# Pocket College Football: New UI Plan

The React rewrite of the game's front end (`ui/`, branch `new-ui`). This file is the source of truth for
what the new UI has, where each old screen goes, and what was decided. **Update it with every change.**

- The old UI and its full screen-by-screen map: `web/`, and the "CFP Coach Simulator Site Map" artifact
  (every old page, view, sub-view and popup with its URL).
- The game itself is JavaScript (`app_js/`, `engine_js/`, `sim_js/`, `career_js/`, `teamdata_js/`) and runs in the app's worker (`public/worker.js`).

## Name and Nav

- The game is called **Pocket College Football** (was "CFP Coach Simulator").
- The header has one nav item: **Play** (was "Coach Career"). Nothing else gets a top-level nav item for now.
- The header's dark side holds only the light/dark toggle (a Phosphor sun/moon icon).

## Routes

`src/router.ts` maps the path to a page (under `ROOT`, the folder the app is opened from). Every screen below is planned
unless its status says otherwise.

| Route           | Screen                         | Old UI                                 | Status      |
| --------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `/`             | Play (start screen)            | Start Screen (`index.html`, no `?id=`) | In progress |
| `/coach/edit`   | Your Coach: create or edit     | `coach.html`                           | In progress |
| `/program/edit` | Custom Program: create or edit | `programs.html`                        | In progress |
| `/program`      | Program overview (maybe)       | None                                   | Tabled      |
| `/play`         | The game: sidebar and sections | `index.html?id=…&tab=…`                | In progress |

### How the Moved Screens Are Reached

- **Your Coach (`/coach/edit`)** is no longer a page in the nav. It shows up:
  - while starting a new career from Play (create a coach, or pick one), and
  - mid-career, when you choose to edit your coach.
- **Custom Programs (`/program/edit`)** is no longer a page in the nav. It shows up:
  - while starting a new career from Play, as an option to make a custom program, and
  - later, as a God Mode option (not now).
- **`/program`** (a team overview) is an idea only. Tabled until we know where it fits in the new-game flow.

## The Game (`/play`): Current State

`src/pages/Game/` with the `GameNav` sidebar (`src/components/GameNav/`); the sections are listed in `src/sections.ts`.
Its own layout: no site header. Address: `/play?id=<season>&section=<key>`. Reached two ways: Your Coach opened for a
team, whose Confirm and Play saves the coach, starts a Coach Career (`POST /api/season` with the team and coach) and
opens it; or a saved season's card under Load Season. Picking a section rewrites the address in place (the rest kept),
so Back leaves the game. A section has no title row (the sidebar names it): its screen fills the space under the
top row and fades in as it opens. The strip's tiles and the coach card share one height and bottom edge.

The sidebar has three modes, like Notion's, remembered by this browser (`cfp.gameNav.mode`, `src/navMode.ts`): open
(Minimize and Hide at the top right), minimized to a rail of icons (names as tooltips; hovering the logo shows
Expand), and hidden (the pointer at the left edge floats it back over the page, with Keep Sidebar Open; the page shows
an Open button at the start of the top row). ⌘\\ / Ctrl+\\ hides and shows it.

## Open Questions

- The new-career flow: in what order do team, league, custom program and coach come? Where does `/program` fit?
- Where do league files come back (import, export)? The League picker was removed from Play until import is supported.
- Where does loading a `.ccsave` career file come back? Saved seasons are under Load Season; deleting a save is not there yet.
- Which God Mode options belong in the new UI, and where.
- Play as a New Program: should it open `/program/edit` directly, or a quick-start step first?
- The old UI draws coaches from `look`; the new one from `face`. Do coaches made in one show up drawn in the other?

## Conventions

- Each component or page is a folder with `index.tsx`, `index.css` and `messages.ts` (all visible text).
- One palette that follows the theme (no fixed dark panel); colors are Notion's neutrals in both themes. Colors, type, spacing and sizes come from `src/globals.css`
  (under 100 lines); fonts from `src/fonts.css`,
  files in `web/fonts/`. Space Mono only.
- Icons: Phosphor (`@phosphor-icons/react`).
- Shared pieces: `EditorPage` for any editor page (sidebar plus main), `FolderTabs` for tabbed panels, `Field` for form
  controls, `useListPopover` for searchable pickers, `Dropdown` for a setting with a few choices, `Tooltip` for what something means on hover, `RecruitStatus` for a recruit's offer or commitment as an icon, `RangeBar` for a read as a range on a track, `ProfileHead` for the head of a player's or recruit's profile, `Panel` (with `Panels` and `PanelRow`) for a titled panel and its rows, `Blocks` for progress as blocks. Reach for these before writing page CSS.
- No Tailwind. CSS class names are `block__element--modifier`.
- Phones (windows narrower than 768 px, `MIN_WIDTH` in `src/viewport.ts`) get the Mobile Not Supported page for every
  address; there is no phone layout.
- Sizes in `px` only (plus `%`, and `vh`/`vw` inside the `clamp()` scales); no `em`, `rem` or `ch`. Stylelint enforces it.
- `npm run check` (Prettier, Stylelint, TypeScript) passes before every commit.
- Copy follows the repo's `CLAUDE.md`: Title Case labels, sentence-case sentences, American spelling.

Four numbers up top (your roster against the limit, how far over, how many are marked, how many cannot be cut), a banner in your color with what is left to do and **Let the Staff Decide** (the game's own rule: the lowest-rated, never a senior or a position at its floor; your marks are kept), then every player you could cut as a card, weakest first: his face and overall, what he gained, what cutting him costs (a Job Promised tag in red, Thin at his position), and Cut or Keep. A marked card steps back and wears a red **Cut stamp** on the corner of his picture. You cannot move on while over the limit, and you may cut more than you must. **This year's signees and transfers cannot be cut** (a folded list under the cards). **A cut is free but for a player you promised a starting job this season**: that breaks the promise and costs your word (`word.apply`). **Where they go**: the cut players, yours and every other school's, are walk-ons a school short at their position takes before it generates one (`offseason._fill_rosters`, which now runs after Roster Cuts); the rest are out of football. Read back from a later stage, the Cuts stage says where each went, his card stamped with the school that took him, and lists anyone another school cut who walked on with you. His story on his card says it too ("Cut by Ohio State. He walked on at Toledo."). **Game logs are the current season's alone**: a past season is its stat line on the player's history; the career no longer keeps five seasons of game-by-game logs for your players (`GAME_LOG_SEASONS` 0), so nothing has to be reconciled when a player is cut or moves. New reusable `Stamp` (the tile a recruit's status wears on a picture's corner, for anything else stamped on a player). The stage is built from the Progress stage's own pieces (the stat tiles with the three-color stripe beneath, the player cards). **The board holds 30** (it was 50 for a day; the player's call). `tests/test_roster_cuts.mjs` covers the class, the stage, the protected newcomers, the staff's cuts, the broken promise, where each player lands, and the Auto path. | 2026-11-19 | A sweep from screenshots. Headquarters: a player's name opens his card (`PlayerLink`), not the Depth Chart. Prospects: Recommended's reasons are off the rows (his hometown again). `Meter` (new): one gray bar that fills in green (`--good`) with its percentage, for Scouted on the recruit file (was `Blocks`). The side marker in your color is gone from `Panel` heads and the section name; every `Panel` and Headquarters card has your three-color stripe along its top instead. `Panels` is rows of two, the panels of a row one height, so edges line up (`split` is now the same layout); Standings' conference cards likewise. A recruit's comp comes from every rostered player (`prospects.player_pool`), not starters only, and his name opens his card. A transfer shows last season's numbers, his games or his last school where a recruit has stars (`transferLine`). `SeasonStrip`: its own eased glide (1100 ms, arrows 500 ms) in place of the browser's smooth scroll; the lift on a new result is gone (it was clipped), its score line holds your color and fades. Recruiting has no top row (week strip and coach card), for the room; Auto-Recruit sits at the end of its tab bar. `ScoutMark` (new): binoculars that fill in green from the left with a prospect's looks (nothing when unscouted), on the board's rows and in the Prospects list's Looks column (was three segments). Headquarters' cards sit in rows, each as tall as its tallest card (was masonry), so their edges line up too. A call or visit's window never scrolls itself, either way (`.modal--talk`): only its log does. The minimized sidebar's team swatch is flat (no tinted shadow, no stripe under it). A complete scouting report drops the Send Scout row (no disabled Report Complete button). The pointer stays an arrow over plain text everywhere (`body` in `globals.css`); only fields show the text cursor. In Recruiting the coach card floats in the window's bottom right corner as your face alone (`CoachBadge` `floating`); hover or focus opens the card with Energy and Auto-Recruit (the tab bar's Auto-Recruit is gone again); it slides out from the right. A sim's week is held until the saved season catches up, so the week strip no longer snaps back and forward when a sim ends. Recruiting: the head's square is His List (your place, #2) and Chance is a cell in words; a board row ends in your place on his list, not a percentage; a board row has his offer icon in its top right corner and "#1 on His List" on a line under his stars. `ProfileHead`'s three cells are always stacked in one column. The floating coach card's text is uncovered by the slide, not faded in. The week's Energy bar (`Energy`, from `CoachBadge`) and the week's Scouting points in the same bar sit at the right end of Recruiting's tab bar; the board's meters are NIL, Offers and Commits on one row. The Snapshot's priorities are three tiles side by side under His Priorities (which priority, the topic, then Your Program: Strong, Fair or Weak, with no bar). The board's list has a search (name, hometown, position), a Position filter beside the stage filter, and a Needs row of chips (the positions your class still has spots at, each a filter). The tools sit on one grid: the search across it, Stage, Position and Sort a third each (all `Dropdown`s), then Class Needs as chips five to a row. Prospects' position chips gain a Show menu: Need, Committed / Need, On Board / Need or Offered / Need. Prospects' table has an Offers column (how many schools have offered him; `offers_n` on the list's rows). A comp is one of the six nearest players, picked by the recruit's own seed (`prospects.COMP_CHOICES`), so a class's best no longer share one comp. Prospects sorts by Offers (`_sort_key` "offers"). The Office's current to-do holds through a sim and moves only once the new week has settled (it flickered between rows as the season and the recruiting hours loaded). The Visited stage has its name back (its tag and group heading were empty). Work Him loses its Pitch dropdown: a message or an offer never used it (the engine drops a pitch on both) and a call or visit picks its topics in its own window. The Office's upcoming game is one row (CCU vs LIB: each side its swatch and abbreviation over its record) and an action's name stays on one line, so the left column fits without a scroll bar. A comp is his name (the link) with his school, position and overall on the line under it. |

| 2026-11-18 | **Headquarters** (`Headquarters`, the old `web/hq.js` and its widgets): a board you build from 31 widgets, in the panel style. Cards pack like a wall of notes into 4 / 2 / 1 columns (Small one column, Medium two, Large the row; `pack` in `index.tsx`), each as tall as its content up to 400 px, then its body scrolls. **Edit Layout** lays the controls over every card: drag it to a new place (the others slide to make room around a dashed placeholder; Escape puts it back), pick its size, move it earlier or later, remove it (with Undo). An empty board offers Start With the Recommended Layout. The layout saves with the career 600 ms after each change (`POST /headquarters`). Each read the cards name is fetched once and shared; an action in a card (Add to Board, Send a Scout, a task, a goal's target) reloads only the reads it changed. Widgets: Class at a Glance, Week's Resources, Top Targets, Class Needs, Visit Schedule, Recent Commits, Recruiting Activity, Commitment Tracker, Hot and Cold Movers, Class Breakdown, Your Full Class, Recruiting Rankings, Recruit Search, Alerts and Needs Attention, Offer Efficiency, Recruiting Calendar, What-If, Recruiting Tasks (with suggested tasks that tick themselves), Recruiting Goals (edit a target in place); Scouting Queue, Flags, Area Scouts, Scouted Players (tiles that open a report in the card), Board Health; Position Battle Board, Scholarship Budget, Player Impact and Retention, Roster Loss Projections, Program Comparison, Next Year's Depth Chart, Promises. A recruit's name opens him on the board (or Prospects when he is not on it); a player's name opens the Depth Chart; View All opens the widget's section. Files: `index.tsx` (the board), `kit.tsx` (Stats, List, Table, Meter, Chart, Tag, Filtered pills), `widgets-recruiting.tsx`, `widgets-program.tsx`, `samples.ts`, `types.ts`.
